title: Determination 2024/018: Refusal to grant a building consent for alterations to replace the external cladding of a dormer roof and window (fire rating of dormer walls)
jurisdiction: New Zealand: Auckland Council as building consent authority; MBIE determination under the Building Act 2004. Non-Alberta comparative record.
code_edition: NZ Building Code (Schedule 1, Building Regulations 1992), with clauses C3.3, C3.6 and C3.7 and section 112(1)(b)(ii) applied. The Acceptable Solution C/AS1 is referred to for external fire spread. No edition is named in the text read.

facts.text: The owner's house is a three-storey townhouse on a flat section in a residential area of Auckland. The two townhouses were built in 2000 under a building consent for which a code compliance certificate was issued.

The second-floor front bedroom has a pushed-out window with a dormer roof. The pushed-out area is 3120 mm wide. Its projection is not measured, but the determination says it would not appear to be more than 500 mm.
The dormer roof is a waterproof membrane over plywood, over building wrap and rafters. The membrane extends down the side walls. The walls are weatherboard-clad.

The distance from the side wall of the push-out to the vertical boundary between the townhouses is approximately 950 mm. The dormer and push-out walls were not originally constructed to provide any fire protection.

Building consent BCO10312543 was applied for on 13 August 2020. At the authority's request the description was amended to a complete reclad, with new weatherboards, new membrane, new deck framing and reconstruction of the roof.

The authority requested that the side walls of the dormer be fully fire rated because the work is new work and must comply with C3.3, C3.6 and C3.7. It said the proposed 18 mm fibre-cement panel fixed directly to framing is not in the James Hardie fire-rated systems.

The owner's position: the work replaces failed cladding and the side walls will continue to comply to the same extent, as section 112(1)(b)(ii) requires. The owner's fire engineer proposed a fibre-cement substrate as an as-near-as-reasonably-practicable solution.
The authority refused the application under section 50 on 12 March 2021 because the issue in its third RFI was not resolved.

limitations: The fire-engineer report and the RFI correspondence are summarised in the determination and are not attached.
The determination limits itself to C3 items (§1.5-1.6). Other Building Code items are outside it.
The projection of the push-out is an estimate in the record (p.3 §2.3).
Owner and street address are omitted.
Applies to the New Zealand Building Code only. No Alberta applicability is asserted.
